message.content: The sea’s hue isn’t fixed—it shifts depending on depth, light conditions, water composition, and even what’s floating above it. In clear shallow waters you’ll often see turquoise or greenish‑blue because sunlight penetrates easily and reflects off sand or algae. Deeper ocean tends toward deep navy or indigo as more wavelengths get absorbed. On bright days over calm seas it looks almost pure azure, while stormy skies or polluted runoff can tint it gray or brown. So “the color of the sea” varies widely—but most people think of it as some shade of blue!
